MG-02.title: Concurrent runner coordination
MG-02.question: With several runner processes against one database, is each migration committed once, does no runner execute it while another is still inside it, and does that survive the loss of any one session of a runner?
MG-02.notes: Each runner is its own OS process and sets application_name to ppcs-A, ppcs-B or ppcs-C. The harness tells those processes apart by that name. It excludes its own connections only when both the backend PID is one of the runner's connections and the name is ppcs-observer. The session ceiling in settings.pool_max applies to each role, not to the sum. A marker's count is how many times the migration committed; a second row of the same marker is that count, not a stray row.

invariants.MG-02.1: After every runner has finished, the migration's marker count is 1 and history holds one entry for it.
invariants.MG-02.2: A runner that did not apply the migration either waited and then found it applied, or reported failure (non-zero exit status).
invariants.MG-02.4: If any single session of runner A ends while A is inside the migration, either A's execution of it does not commit, or no other runner executes it before A finishes: its marker count is 1. Judged only when the session actually ended; otherwise the case is INCONCLUSIVE.
invariants.MG-02.5: No runner starts executing the migration while another runner's execution of it is still live (its session still inside the migration): two live sessions inside it at once is a violation.

MG-03.title: Rollback and history consistency
MG-03.question: After a revert, does history describe the database, and is a migration without a reversal ever reported as reversed?

invariants.MG-03.1: If a revert reports a migration as reverted, its history entry is absent and its marker is absent.
invariants.MG-03.2: If a migration provides no reversal, a revert does not report it as reverted while its marker remains: it refuses before changing history, or follows a documented irreversible-migration contract that keeps history and database consistent.
invariants.MG-03.3: If a migration's reversal fails, the operation reports failure and the migration's history entry remains; for a transactional migration, its marker also remains.

cases.title: Runner B starts while runner A is inside the migration
steps: The runner holds advisory lock K on its own session.
Runner A applies { m1 }. m1 inserts its marker, then waits on select pg_advisory_xact_lock(K), inside the migration's transaction.
Checkpoint inside-A: A's session is waiting for K.
Runner B applies { m1 }. For the bound, B may exit, reach the gate, or stay blocked on the framework's own coordination.
Release K. A and B finish within the deadline. Runner C applies { m1 }.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the last runner has returned: the runner records the state at report time.
cases.knowledge: A runner that waits learns that another run is in progress. It does not learn, from a successful return alone, that its own execution was the one that committed.

cases.title: Two runners released together against a database with no history storage
steps: Runners A and B each connect and wait at a start barrier. The database has no history storage.
Release both at once. A runner that executes m1 waits at the gate K.
For the bound, each runner may exit, reach the gate, or wait on the framework's own coordination. Then release K and require both to finish within the deadline.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as both runners have returned: the runner records the state at report time.
cases.knowledge: Neither runner can see, before it starts, that the other is about to apply the same migration. The database starts with no history row that could tell it so.

cases.title: One session of runner A ends while A is inside the migration
steps: As MG-02.held, until checkpoint inside-A.
List runner A's sessions by application_name ppcs-A. Terminate one of them with pg_terminate_backend. The choice does not depend on which session holds the framework's lock.
Runner B applies { m1 }. For the bound, B may exit, reach the gate, or stay blocked on the framework's own coordination.
Release K. A and B finish within the deadline. Runner C applies { m1 }.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the last runner has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

fault.mechanism: pg_terminate_backend() of one session of runner A, chosen by application_name ppcs-A, without knowing which session coordinates.
fault.injection_point: While A's migration waits at the gate, after its marker insert.
fault.expected_server: The session ends. Session-scoped locks it held are released. Its open transaction, if any, aborts.
fault.expected_client: The client of that session sees the connection drop.

cases.knowledge: The runner whose session ended can see the connection error. Another runner cannot see, from the database alone, that the ended session was the one holding coordination.

cases.title: PostgreSQL ends runner A's idle sessions while A is inside the migration
steps: Runner A's connections set idle_session_timeout = 1s.
As MG-02.held, until checkpoint inside-A.
Wait until one of A's sessions has ended, or 4 s have passed.
Runner B applies { m1 }. For the bound, B may exit, reach the gate, or stay blocked on the framework's own coordination.
Release K. A and B finish within the deadline. Runner C applies { m1 }.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the last runner has returned: the runner records the state at report time.
cases.knowledge: idle_session_timeout ends a session that is idle outside a transaction. A session busy inside the migration's transaction is not idle, so the setting does not end that session.

cases.title: A migration whose reversal deletes its marker
steps: Runner A applies { m1 }. m1 inserts marker m1.
Revert with the framework's default selection. m1's reversal deletes marker m1.
Apply { m1 } again.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the revert has returned and the reapply has returned: the runner records the state at report time.
cases.knowledge: A reported revert says the migration's effects are gone. The next apply is what shows that history and the database agree: the migration runs again.

cases.title: A migration that provides no reversal is reverted
steps: Runner A applies { m1 }. m1 inserts marker m1 and provides no reversal.
Revert with the framework's default selection.
Apply { m1 } again.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the revert has returned and the reapply has returned: the runner records the state at report time.
cases.knowledge: The caller of revert learns only what the operation reports. If that report says the migration was reverted, the caller treats its effects as gone.

cases.title: A transactional migration's reversal deletes its marker and then fails
steps: Runner A applies { m1 }.
Revert. m1's reversal deletes its marker and then raises an error. The migration is transactional, so the deletion is in the reversal's transaction.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the revert has returned: the runner records the state at report time.
cases.knowledge: A reported failure says the revert did not complete. For a transactional migration, the caller can treat the migration as still applied.
